caption:
This morning: Uber is giving ChatGPT Work to all 30,000 employees, up from a 1,000-person pilot. No results have been reported yet.

The deep dive: the default model costs $10 per million output tokens against $50 for Astra. Enterprise seats are reportedly around $60 a month, with no list price. And 40% of developer reactions are skeptical.

My take: the model cost is the small part. Measure which workflows actually changed.

Comment PROJECT and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning I covered Uber giving ChatGPT Work to all 30,000 employees after a 1,000-person pilot. Then I went back in to check the numbers around it.
First, the default model, GPT-6.1 Sol, charges ten dollars per million output tokens. Astra charges fifty, so the cost per task drops sharply.
Second, Enterprise seats have no list price, but buyers report around sixty dollars a month, against twenty for Business.
Third, early developer reactions to the rollout are split: forty percent skeptical, forty-five mixed, fifteen positive.
My take: the model cost is the small part. Pay for seats and tokens, then measure which workflows actually changed.
